_note: Expert trees, M13. Every node moves its own class's power and nothing else: `tunes` names a knob the power declares, `grants` names a rule the power is kin to, `gives_ench` names an ench inside the licence. `expert_nodes_touch_only_the_expert` is the lint. Six nodes a tree, two points a node, ten trees, sixty nodes.

nodes.name: The Rate Card
nodes.blurb: Pinned inside the funnel where the light is worst. Two figures, one crossed out, and the crossing-out is the older of the two.

nodes.name: Standing Order
nodes.blurb: Thirty points a fight, drawn whether you need them. Twenty-two fights in, nobody has needed all thirty and nobody has cancelled it.

nodes.name: The Overdraft
nodes.blurb: You may go twenty past empty. You may not go to nothing; the last point of you is not for sale and the clerk has that in writing.

nodes.name: The Rebate
nodes.blurb: A kill inside the fight refunds half the bill, paid at the bell, in strength, in front of whoever is left.

nodes.name: Shouted Figures
nodes.blurb: He shouts the exchange rate over the noise and the rate improves each time he shouts it. Four shouts is where it stops improving.

nodes.name: Both Books Open
nodes.blurb: One for one. The Sergeant stops arguing at one for one, which took eleven years and a funnel.

nodes.name: The Count
nodes.blurb: Three items. The fourth is what makes a fact an opinion, and nobody has explained why.

nodes.name: The First Fact
nodes.blurb: One fact, held open, for as long as you are carrying little enough to hold it.

nodes.name: Writ in the Margin
nodes.blurb: A fact that cannot expire is read more often, and reading it costs the reader.

nodes.name: The Second Fact
nodes.blurb: Two at once. The Keeper kept nine at once for a season and was asked to stop by six people who had all been counted.

nodes.name: Bare-Armed
nodes.blurb: Four items and the fact still stands. Past four it sits down.

nodes.name: Told Again
nodes.blurb: A fact that outlives the fight is told to the next thing you meet, once, before it has said anything.

nodes.name: Dry Bearing
nodes.blurb: An empty frame has nothing in it to slow down. Kaklon called this obvious in 1911 and nobody has built on it since.

nodes.name: The Empty Bench
nodes.blurb: Six more turns of nothing, banked. The bench does not know it is empty.

nodes.name: The Clearing
nodes.blurb: Every second turn, the bare cell next to worked ground becomes worked ground. Four turns is four cells and the frame is not empty any more, only unpacked.

nodes.name: Counterspin
nodes.blurb: Two stacks survive an activation. The arm does not stop; it is asked to pause and it declines twice.

nodes.name: Both Arms
nodes.blurb: A whole stack a turn off a frame with nothing in it. Twelve turns is twelve, which is more than most people manage with gear on.

nodes.name: Overwound
nodes.blurb: Sixteen over the old ceiling and it turns faster than that. The recall notice for this one is printed under the tap.

nodes.name: The Poster
nodes.blurb: Sixty percent, printed. The printer got it wrong and the house honoured the print, and has honoured it every night since.

nodes.name: Quick Change
nodes.blurb: Two seconds an empty frame. Five empty frames is ten seconds, which is the whole of the original window and the reason the window was ten.

nodes.name: The House Clock
nodes.blurb: Two seconds slow since 1904. Every act in the building is paid off it and no act has complained.

nodes.name: The Second House
nodes.blurb: Each paid win adds a second to the next window, up to five. A win outside the window puts it back to nothing.

nodes.name: No Encore
nodes.blurb: Fifteen points more for the act that does not come back out. The house has counted eleven encores in nine seasons and paid for none of them.

nodes.name: The Short Programme Itself
nodes.blurb: Twice the bill on a fast win with nothing on. The judges gave it a five, a two and a minus seven, and the box office does not read scores.

nodes.name: The Form
nodes.blurb: Five a fight. There is a box for a sixth and the box has never been filled in by anyone the Keeper will name.

nodes.name: Ripest First
nodes.blurb: Spend the one with the least time left rather than the cheapest. The clerk fought this for two years on the grounds that it was sensible.

nodes.name: Countersigned
nodes.blurb: Every third requisition puts the curse back where it was found, signed twice, still running.

nodes.name: Two Signatures
nodes.blurb: A spent curse covers half again what a cast costs, and the half again is banked rather than lost.

nodes.name: Standing Requisition
nodes.blurb: Eight a fight. The Sergeant signs the whole book at the start and hands it over open.

nodes.name: The Whole Book
nodes.blurb: Every second one comes back, and each covers double. The requisition is now cheaper than the cast, which the Sergeant says is how requisitions are meant to work.

nodes.name: The Tap
nodes.blurb: Eight a stack a turn. The tap is on the side of the funnel and the side of the funnel is the patent's, so the eight is licensed.

nodes.name: The Second Licence
nodes.blurb: It turns every eight hundred milliseconds instead of every thousand. Two hundred milliseconds, bought and paid for, twelve times a fight.

nodes.name: Full Rows
nodes.blurb: A row with no gap in it pays four a cell at the bell, and stays exactly where it is. Nothing clears; the row is the machine and clearing it would be taking the machine apart.

nodes.name: The Flywheel Brake
nodes.blurb: Two stacks survive the activation. A brake that keeps the wheel turning is what the patent office queried and what the patent says.

nodes.name: The Overflow Pipe
nodes.blurb: Funny past the top of the funnel comes out as armour, one for one, down a pipe added in 1912 by somebody who was tired of mopping.

nodes.name: The Funnel, Patented
nodes.blurb: Twelve a stack a turn and the rows pay half again. Spike Kaklon has offered nine hundred Fnorp for the drawings on four occasions.

nodes.name: Longer Overture
nodes.blurb: Thirteen seconds. Three of them are the conductor deciding whether to start.

nodes.name: The Standing Discount
nodes.blurb: Twenty percent off after the window closes, on the grounds that the house is already warm.

nodes.name: Encore
nodes.blurb: A kill inside the window starts the window again. Once. The house has a rule about twice and the rule is the number two.

nodes.name: Unspent
nodes.blurb: Funny left over when the lights come up lands as armour. Nobody at the house can explain the mechanism and the armour is on you regardless.

nodes.name: Second Overture
nodes.blurb: Seventeen seconds. The programme lists it as four minutes and the programme is not the clock.

nodes.name: The Whole First Act
nodes.blurb: Two encores and half price after. Eleven seasons of first acts and the second act has been performed nine times.

nodes.name: The Searing Clause
nodes.blurb: Clause four. The weapon frame, every time it goes off, and the ench does not have to be told which weapon.

nodes.name: The Frost Clause
nodes.blurb: Clause seven, added when a licensee held both hands out and asked what the gloves were for.

nodes.name: Second Reading
nodes.blurb: Every third activation of an enched item lands its curse twice, and the item runs fifteen percent slower for the privilege. The office reads everything twice and takes longer.

nodes.name: The Stun Rider
nodes.blurb: A rider on the helmet, in a hand nobody at the office recognises, initialled by three people who have all left.

nodes.name: The Misfire Schedule
nodes.blurb: Schedule two, the greaves. Every third act of theirs does nothing, which the schedule describes as an administrative outcome.

nodes.name: The Licence Entire
nodes.blurb: Twice a curse on every enched activation, every clause, every frame. It is nine pages and eight of them are the list.

nodes.name: The Ledger Column
nodes.blurb: Fifteen percent a curse, in a column the Keeper added and the box office has never queried.

nodes.name: The House Count
nodes.blurb: Six counted instead of four. The two extra were being landed anyway and now they are being paid for.

nodes.name: Four Kinds
nodes.blurb: Four different kinds on one fallen creature pays double. Three kinds pays what three kinds pays, which is the point of the number four.

nodes.name: The Long Run
nodes.blurb: A curse that ran out before the bell counts for half. It was on them for most of it and the ledger says so.

nodes.name: The Billing Review
nodes.blurb: Twenty percent a curse. Reviewed in the eighth season, upheld in the ninth, reviewed again out of habit.

nodes.name: Eleven Seasons of It
nodes.blurb: Thirty percent a curse and nine of them counted. The act has not changed since the second season and the money has changed eleven times.

nodes.name: The Second Rack
nodes.blurb: Three a component. The rack was built for two and has four slots, which is the sort of thing the workshop did.

nodes.name: The Standing Order
nodes.blurb: The Index, off the house list, no charge. It has been on the list since the list was one item long.

nodes.name: Ponkey Broadcast
nodes.blurb: An enched component lends forty percent of what it is carrying to every finished item touching it. The lending is not noticed by the lender.

nodes.name: The House List
nodes.blurb: The Allowance, which the house has never charged for and has twice tried to stop giving away.

nodes.name: Wider Broadcast
nodes.blurb: Sixty-five percent, and it reaches diagonally now, which the workshop insists is the same thing.

nodes.name: The Bill in Full
nodes.blurb: Four a component and eighty percent lent out. Two licences, one rack, and a bill that runs to a second page.
